speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are suffering from severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly where you feel the pain the most?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

Given the history of dyspareunia, dysuria, and severe abdominal pain in a sexually active 17-year-old, I need to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Chlamydia/Gonorrhea NAAT, and CBC with differential. Please also provide the results of any pelvic examination performed.
